Other options: Repatriation = the return of someone to his country; Pedestrian = A person who is walking in a city, along a road, etc; Illiterate = A person who cannot read or write.
Journeys especially by a group of people for a specific purpose

Expedition = Journeys especially by a group of people for a specific purpose. Hindi: अभियान. Example: The scientific expedition aimed to explore uncharted territories. Other options: Illustration = pictures given in a book for the purpose of explaining things; Congregation = A group of worshippers; Generic = not specific.
To make atonement for one's sins

Expiate = To make atonement for one's sins. Hindi: प्रायश्चित करना. Example: He sought to expiate his guilt by performing acts of kindness. Other options: Placate = make someone less angry or hostile; Expanse = A large open area of land, water or sky; Prevaricate = to make evasive or misleading statements.

Expire = To come to an end. Hindi: समाप्त होना. Example: The contract will expire at the end of the month. Other options: Abolish = formally put an end to a system; Deluge = large amount of things that come at the same time; Expiate = to make atonement for one's sins.

Exposition = An act of explaining something. Hindi: व्याख्या. Example: The opening chapter provided essential exposition for the complex plot. Other options: Disaster = an act that has disastrous consequences; Restitution = an act of returning something that was lost or stolen to its owner; Dereliction = an act of no longer caring for, using, or doing something, failure to do….

Extempore = Spoken or done without preparation. Hindi: बिना तैयारी के. Example: She spoke extempore at the conference without any prepared notes. Other options: Impromptu = made or done without preparation; Extortion = crime of getting money from someone by the use of force or threat; Extradite = sending (a person who has been accused of a crime) to another state or….

Extinguish = Stop something from burning. Hindi: बुझाना. Example: The firefighter worked tirelessly to extinguish the raging fire. Other options: Linguist = A person who knows several foreign languages well; Insulated = covered with a material or substance in order to stop heat or sound from…; Inextinguishable = that which can not be put out.
Crime of getting money from someone by the use of force or threat

Extortion = Crime of getting money from someone by the use of force or threat. Hindi: ज़बरदस्ती वसूली. Example: The criminal used threats to obtain money through extortion. Other options: Oration = A formal speech, especially one given on a ceremonial occasion; Requisition = asking for or demanding and taking (something) for one's use; Coercion = use of force or threats to get someone to agree to something.
A lively and confident person who enjoys being with other people

Extrovert = A lively and confident person who enjoys being with other people. Hindi: बहिर्मुखी. Example: Her outgoing and sociable nature made her a true extrovert. Other options: Extradite = sending (a person who has been accused of a crime) to another state or…; Extravagant = A person who wastes money on luxury; Subvert = secretly try to ruin or destroy a government, political system, etc.

Facet = Parts or elements of something. Hindi: पहलू. Example: Each facet of the diamond sparkled in the sunlight. Other options: Heterogeneous = made up of parts that are different; Ruins = the broken parts of objects found in an ancient site; Multitudinous = consisting of many things or parts.

Facile = Performing adroitly and without effort. Hindi: सुगम. Example: His facile explanations failed to address the complexity of the issue. Other options: Prima Facie = based on what is known or seen when something is first considered or dealt…; Facsimile = an exact copy of handwriting or picture produced by a machine; Faction = groups within a larger group that have different ideas and opinions than the rest….
An exact copy of handwriting or picture produced by a machine

Facsimile = An exact copy of handwriting or picture produced by a machine. Hindi: प्रतिकृति. Example: The old letter was preserved as a digital facsimile. Other options: Output = an amount of something that is produced by a person or thing; Facile = performing adroitly and without effort; Counterfeit = made to look like an exact copy of something in order to trick people.
Groups within a larger group that have different ideas and opinions than the rest of the group

Faction = Groups within a larger group that have different ideas and opinions than the rest of the group. Hindi: गुट. Example: The political party split into rival factions with differing ideologies. Other options: Expedition = journeys especially by a group of people for a specific purpose; Tenet = beliefs or ideas that are very important to a group; Connotation = ideas suggested by a word in addition to its main meaning.
A thing that is not genuine

Fake = A thing that is not genuine. Hindi: नकली. Example: The antique vase turned out to be a cleverly crafted fake. Other options: Monomania = obsession with one particular thing; Edible = A thing that can be eaten; Output = an amount of something that is produced by a person or thing.
One who is subject to failure

Fallible = One who is subject to failure. Hindi: भूल करने योग्य. Example: Despite his expertise, he acknowledged that he was fallible and could make mistakes. Other options: Summary = A brief account of a subject; Mortality = the state of being subject to death; Indelible = making marks that cannot be removed.

Fanatical = Marked by extreme enthusiasm. Hindi: कट्टर. Example: Her fanatical devotion to the cause sometimes bordered on obsession. Other options: Nyctophobia = an extreme fear of darkness; Cynophobia = extreme fear of dogs; Radical = A person who advocates complete political or social change.
Ideas about doing something that is far removed from normal reality

Fantasy = Ideas about doing something that is far removed from normal reality. Hindi: कल्पना. Example: He escaped into the world of fantasy novels to forget his troubles. Other options: Apostasy = the state of having rejected your religious beliefs or your political party; Fanatic = one who is filled with excessive enthusiasm in religious matters; Amputee = A person who has had one or more limbs removed.
Funny plays or movies about ridiculous situations

Farce = Funny plays or movies about ridiculous situations. Hindi: स्वांग. Example: The chaotic comedy of errors turned the play into a hilarious farce. Other options: Precedent = A previous case that might serve as an example or guide in subsequent situations; Facet = parts or elements of something; Sarcasm = use of words that mean the opposite of what one really wants to say….
One who is much concerned about details and accuracy

Fastidious = One who is much concerned about details and accuracy. Hindi: नकचढ़ा. Example: She was fastidious about cleanliness and organisation. Other options: Loquacious = one who loves to speak; Fatalist = one who believes in fate; Ambidextrous = one who can use either hand with ease.
Causing or ending in a death

Fatal = Causing or ending in a death. Hindi: घातक. Example: The accident had a fatal outcome. Other options: Suicide = act of intentionally causing one's own death; Disband = ending an organisation or group (such as a club); Innocuous = causing no harm.
The belief that events are decided by fate and you can not control them

Fatalism = The belief that events are decided by fate and you can not control them. Hindi: नियतिवाद. Example: His belief in fatalism led him to accept whatever fate had in store. Other options: Pacifism = belief that war and violence are unjustified; Imperialism = the policy of extending a country's empire and influence; Provincialism = concern for one's own area or region at the expense of national or supranational….

Fatalist = One who believes in fate. Hindi: भाग्यवादी. Example: As a fatalist, he believed that whatever happened was beyond human control. Other options: Monotheist = one who believes in the theory of only one god; Funambulist = one who walks on ropes; Journalist = A person who writes for newspapers and magazines.

Faux Pas = Embarrassing social mistake. Hindi: सामाजिक चूक. Example: Making that social faux pas left her feeling embarrassed. Other options: Solecism = A minor mistake in grammar or social behaviour; Gregarious = loves being social and enjoys the company of others; Erratum = A mistake in a book.
That is possible and likely to be achieved

Feasible = That is possible and likely to be achieved. Hindi: संभव. Example: The ambitious project seemed daunting, but it was feasible with proper planning. Other options: Edible = A thing that can be eaten; Volatile = likely to change in a very sudden or extreme way; likely to become dangerous…; Plausible = seeming reasonable.
An act of committing a serious crime such as murder or rape

Felony = An act of committing a serious crime such as murder or rape. Hindi: घोर अपराध. Example: Committing a serious crime could result in a felony charge. Other options: Exposition = an act of explaining something; Mutiny = an act of refusing to obey the orders of somebody in authority; Fraud = an act of deceiving somebody in order to make money.
One who believes in giving equal opportunity to women in all fields

Feminist = One who believes in giving equal opportunity to women in all fields. Hindi: नारीवादी. Example: A committed feminist, she campaigned tirelessly for equal pay. Other options: Benefactor = one who helps people by giving them money or other aid; Philogynist = A person who likes or admires women; Polytheist = one who believes in many gods.
A boat or ship for conveying passengers and goods

Fete = Large parties or celebrations. Hindi: उत्सव. Example: The town celebrated with a lively fete. Other options: Coalition = governments formed by two or more political parties working together; Confederacy = the union of states, parties or persons; Horde = A large group of people.
Destruction or abortion of a foetus

Foeticide = Destruction or abortion of a foetus. Hindi: भ्रूणहत्या. Example: The illegal act of intentionally causing the death of a foetus is called foeticide. Long and angry fights or quarrels between two people or two groups

Feud = Long and angry fights or quarrels between two people or two groups. Hindi: झगड़ा. Example: The long-standing feud between the families finally ended with a peace treaty. Fictitious = Imagined, not real. Hindi: काल्पनिक. Example: The novel's characters were entirely fictitious, created by the author's imagination. Other options: Conceivable = capable of being imagined or grasped mentally; Bona Fide = genuine, real or legal; not false; Ostentatious = displaying wealth, knowledge, etc., in a way that is meant to attract attention, admiration,….
Persons who are very enthusiastic about something

Fiend = Persons who are very enthusiastic about something. Hindi: शौकीन. Example: The serial killer was a fiend who terrorised the city. Other options: Greenhorn = persons who lack experience and knowledge; Heartily = in an enthusiastic way; Envoy = persons who are sent by one government to represent it in dealing with another….
Something that is imagined but does not exist

Figment = Something that is imagined but does not exist. Hindi: मनगढ़ंत. Example: The ghostly figure he saw in the old mansion turned out to be a mere figment of his imagination. Other options: Interment = an act of burying a dead person; Fictitious = imagined, not real; Vehement = showing strong feeling.
Killing of one's son or daughter

Filicide = Killing of one's son or daughter. Hindi: संतान-हत्या. Example: The horrifying act of a parent killing their own child is known as filicide. Other options: Mariticide = the killing of one's husband; Patricide = the killing of a father; Avicide = killing of birds.
Large and very unpleasant amount of dirt

Filth = Large and very unpleasant amount of dirt. Hindi: गंदगी. Example: The neglected alley was filled with garbage and filth. Other options: Ominous = suggesting that something unpleasant is likely to happen; Onerous = difficult and unpleasant to do or deal with; Horrendous = something that is extremely unpleasant.
Best or most important thing owned or produced by a particular organisation

Flagship = Best or most important thing owned or produced by a particular organisation. Hindi: प्रमुख. Example: The latest smartphone model is the company's flagship product. Other options: Scholarship = A grant of payment to support a student's education; Subsidiary = not as important as something else; Numero Uno = best or most important person or thing.
Groups of military ships commanded by the same person

Fleet = Groups of military ships commanded by the same person. Hindi: बेड़ा. Example: The delivery company had a large fleet of trucks for transporting goods. Other options: Species = groups of animals or plants that are similar and can produce young animals or…; Entourage = groups of people who go with and assist an important person; Crew = groups of people who operate a ship, aeroplane, or train.
Shine with a bright but brief or irregular light

Flicker = Shine with a bright but brief or irregular light. Hindi: झिलमिलाहट. Example: The candle's flicker danced in the dark. Other options: Illuminate = to brighten up with light; Summary = A brief account of a subject; Sojourn = A brief or short stay at a place.

Flip side = Unwelcome aspect of a situation. Hindi: दूसरा पहलू. Example: The flip side of success is hard work. Other options: Cohort = groups of people who share a common feature or aspect of behaviour; Sanguine = optimistic in an apparently difficult situation; Imbroglio = complex situation or a mix-up.
A group of birds of one kind

Flock = A group of birds of one kind. Hindi: झुंड. Example: A flock of birds soared gracefully across the sky. Other options: Triumvirate = A group of three people holding power together; Caravan = A group of people, typically with vehicles or animals travelling together; Choir = A group of singers in a church.

Flog = Beat or whip (someone) severely. Hindi: चाबुक से मारना. Example: In the past, soldiers were flogged for disobedience. Other options: Flock = A group of birds of one kind; Backlog = quantities of work that should have been done already, but has not yet been…; Flotilla = A small fleet of ships or boats.
All the plants that live in a particular area, time, period, or environment

Flora = All the plants that live in a particular area, time, period, or environment. Hindi: वनस्पतिजात. Example: The flora of the rainforest is incredibly diverse. Other options: Fauna = the animals living in an area or in a particular period of time; Contemporary = existing or happening in the same time period; Depreciate = to become less valuable over a period of time.
A person who sells and arranges cut flowers

Florist = A person who sells and arranges cut flowers. Hindi: फूलवाला. Example: She visited the local florist to pick out a bouquet for her friend's birthday. Other options: Arsonist = A person who deliberately sets fire to a building; Pessimist = A person who always expects bad things to happen; Flora = all the plants that live in a particular area, time, period, or environment.
A small fleet of ships or boats

Flotilla = A small fleet of ships or boats. Hindi: छोटी नावों का बेड़ा. Example: The naval flotilla consisted of several small warships patrolling the coastal waters. Other options: Pendant = A small ornament which hangs down especially from a necklace; Podium = A small raised platform for a speaker, conductor or winner; Armada = fleet of warships.

Flux = Series of changes. Hindi: प्रवाह. Example: The constant changes in technology created a state of flux in the industry. Other options: Vicissitude = many changes or problems that happen over time; Efflux = materials that are flowing out; Gamut = range or series of related things.
Ideas or stories that are not true but that many people have heard or read

Folklore = Ideas or stories that are not true but that many people have heard or read. Hindi: लोक-साहित्य. Example: The ancient folklore told tales of mythical creatures and heroic deeds. Other options: Audible = that can be heard easily; Lore = the traditional knowledge, beliefs, and stories that relate to a particular place, subject, or…; Discord = lack of agreements between people, ideas, etc.
Go or come after a person or thing proceeding ahead

Follow = Go or come after a person or thing proceeding ahead. Hindi: अनुसरण करना. Example: She decided to follow her passion and pursue a career in art. Other options: Expire = to come to an end; Output = an amount of something that is produced by a person or thing; Folklore = ideas or stories that are not true but that many people have heard or….
An ability to see what will or might happen in the future

Foresight = An ability to see what will or might happen in the future. Hindi: दूरदर्शिता. Example: His foresight allowed him to plan for potential challenges in advance. Other options: Oracy = an ability to express oneself well in speech; Posterity = people in the future; Pessimism = feelings or beliefs that bad things will happen in the future.
Be deprived of a property or a right

Forfeited = Be deprived of a property or a right. Hindi: जब्त. Example: He forfeited his right to the prize by violating the rules. Other options: Discretion = the right to choose what should be done in a particular situation; Bequeath = leaving (property) to a person or other beneficiary by a will; Disenfranchisement = the state of being deprived of a right or privilege.

Forgery = Falsification of documents etc. Hindi: जालसाजी. Example: The detective uncovered a sophisticated forgery ring selling fake antiques. Other options: Fortnight = A period of two weeks; Archive = collection of historical documents or records providing information about a place, institution, or group…; Fortuitous = something that is to your advantage but happened by chance.

Forthcoming = Appearing, happening, or arriving soon. Hindi: आगामी. Example: The author promised a forthcoming sequel to the popular novel. Other options: Consequent = happening as a result of something; Contemporary = existing or happening in the same time period; Fortnight = A period of two weeks.
Something that is to your advantage but happened by chance

Fortuitous = Something that is to your advantage but happened by chance. Hindi: आकस्मिक. Example: The meeting was a fortuitous coincidence. Other options: Momentous = very important or serious; Privilege = right or advantage available to a person; Ubiquitous = seeming to be seen everywhere.

Fracas = Noisy arguments or fights. Hindi: हंगामा. Example: The heated argument escalated into a noisy fracas in the crowded bar. Other options: Fraud = an act of deceiving somebody in order to make money; Altercation = noisy arguments or disagreements, especially in public; Fragile = something which can be easily broken.

Franchise = Constitutional right to cast vote. Hindi: मताधिकार. Example: The fast-food restaurant expanded its franchise to other cities. Other options: Privilege = right or advantage available to a person; Fratricide = the killing of one's brother; Stanchion = an upright bar, post, or frame forming a support or barrier.
Groups of people who have the same job, interests, etc

Fraternity = Groups of people who have the same job, interests, etc. Hindi: बिरादरी. Example: The college fraternity held social events. Other options: Platoon = groups of people who are doing something together; Consortium = groups of people, companies, etc., that agree to work together; Audience = groups of people who have gathered to watch or listen to something (a play,….

Fratricide = The killing of one's brother. Hindi: भ्रातृहत्या. Example: The civil war was marked by fratricide, as brothers fought on opposite sides. Other options: Mariticide = the killing of one's husband; Infanticide = the killing of a newborn child; Homicide = the killing of a human being.
Great and often wild or uncontrolled activities

Frenzy = Great and often wild or uncontrolled activities. Hindi: उन्माद. Example: The black Friday shoppers moved in a frenzy, grabbing discounted items. Other options: Hiatus = periods of time when something (activities or programmes) are stopped; Delirium = mental states in which one is confused and not able to think or speak…; Revel = take great pleasure.

Frivolous = Not deserving serious attention. Hindi: तुच्छ. Example: The lawsuit was dismissed as frivolous, lacking any substantial evidence. Other options: Heed = pay attention; Credulous = A person who is too ready to believe others; Exemplary = extremely good and deserving to be admired and copied.
The feeling of being upset or annoyed as a result of being unable to change or achieve something

Frustration = The feeling of being upset or annoyed as a result of being unable to change or achieve something. Hindi: निराशा. Example: His repeated failures led to feelings of frustration and disappointment. Other options: Respiration = the process by means of which plants and animals breathe; Alliteration = repetition of an initial sound in two or more words in a line; Illustration = pictures given in a book for the purpose of explaining things.
One who runs away from justice

Fugitive = One who runs away from justice. Hindi: भगोड़ा. Example: The fugitive evaded capture for three weeks before being apprehended. Other options: Vindictive = having or showing a desire to hurt someone who has hurt or caused problems…; Sensitive = aware of and able to understand other people and their feelings; Laxative = A medicine that softens the bowels.

Fumbling = Doing something in clumsy manner. Hindi: टटोलना. Example: His nervousness caused him to drop the keys while fumbling to unlock the door. Other options: Platoon = groups of people who are doing something together; Appalling = causing shock or dismay; Jauntily = having or expressing a lively, cheerful, and self-confident manner.

Funambulist = One who walks on ropes. Hindi: रस्सी पर चलनेवाला नट. Example: The daring funambulist walked the tightrope. Other options: Fatalist = one who believes in fate; Somnambulist = someone who walks in sleep; Misologist = one who hates reason, argument, or enlightenment.
Ceremony held for a dead person

Funeral = Ceremony held for a dead person. Hindi: अंतिम संस्कार. Example: Friends and family gathered to pay their respects at the sombre funeral. Other options: Bicameral = A legislative body having two chambers; Unilateral = involving only one group or country; Convocation = ceremony held in a university or college when students receive their degrees.
Simple fast spreading plant without flowers or leaves which often can create disease

Fungus = Simple fast spreading plant without flowers or leaves which often can create disease. Hindi: कुकुरमुत्ता. Example: The damp basement was infested with mould and fungus. Other options: Florist = A person who sells and arranges cut flowers; Humus = the organic component of soil, formed by the decomposition of leaves and other plant…; Funambulist = one who walks on ropes.
The main body of an aircraft

Fuselage = The main body of an aircraft. Hindi: हवाई जहाज़ का ढांचा. Example: The aeroplane's fuselage housed the passengers and cargo. Other options: Physiology = A study of the human body; Downtown = main or central part of a city or town; Auxiliary = giving help or support to the main group of workers.
An activity or excitement that is unusual and that often is not wanted or necessary

Fuss = An activity or excitement that is unusual and that often is not wanted or necessary. Hindi: गड़बड़. Example: The bride's mother made a fuss over every detail of the wedding. Other options: Indispensable = A person who is absolutely necessary for someone or something; Bizarre = very strange or unusual; Mimicry = an activity or art of copying the behaviour or speech of other people.

Gait = A particular way of walking. Hindi: चाल. Example: The doctor observed the patient's gait carefully, noting a slight limp. Other options: Dialect = A particular form of a language which is peculiar to a specific region; Cuisine = food that is cooked in a particular way, style of cooking; Somnambulism = walking in sleep.
A brave, noble-minded or chivalrous man

Gallant = A brave, noble-minded or chivalrous man. Hindi: वीर. Example: The gallant knight bowed before the queen and pledged his service. Other options: Henpeck = A man who is controlled by his wife; Widower = A man whose wife is dead; Adonis = an extremely handsome young man.

Galling = Causing annoyance and resentment. Hindi: कष्टदायक. Example: It was galling to lose the championship by a single point after months of training. Other options: Gallant = A brave, noble-minded or chivalrous man; Chagrin = annoyance or distress at having failed or been humiliated; Fatal = causing or ending in a death.
An act or remark that is calculated to gain an advantage

Gambit = An act or remark that is calculated to gain an advantage. Hindi: पहला क़दम. Example: His opening gambit in the negotiation was to offer a lower price than expected. Other options: Disaster = an act that has disastrous consequences; Ploy = clever trick or plan that is used to get someone to do something or…; Felony = an act of committing a serious crime such as murder or rape.
Range or series of related things

Gamut = Range or series of related things. Hindi: सरगम. Example: The report covered the full gamut of issues from poverty to climate change. Other options: Trilogy = series of three novels, movies, etc., that are closely related and involve the same…; Lunar = related to the moon; Saga = long and complicated series of events.
Journals or newspapers, especially the official one of an organisation or institution

Gazette = Journals or newspapers, especially the official one of an organisation or institution. Hindi: राज-पत्र. Example: The appointment was published in the official gazette. Other options: Etiquette = the customary code of polite behaviour in society; Netiquette = rules about the proper and polite way to communicate with other people when one…; Ethos = guiding beliefs of a person, group, or organisation.
A line of descent traced continuously from an ancestor

Genealogy = A line of descent traced continuously from an ancestor. Hindi: वंशावली. Example: She traced her genealogy back five generations using old church records. Generic = Not specific. Hindi: सामान्य. Example: The doctor prescribed a generic version of the drug to reduce costs. Other options: Gentry = people of high social status; Expedition = journeys especially by a group of people for a specific purpose; Alphanumeric = consisting of or using both letters and numerals.

Genesis = Beginning or origin of something. Hindi: उत्पत्ति. Example: The genesis of the conflict lay in decades of territorial disputes. Other options: Adolescence = the beginning of puberty; Nemesis = opponents or enemies that are very difficult to defeat; Antithesis = persons or things that are the direct opposite of someone or something else.
The killing of a whole race

Genocide = The killing of a whole race. Hindi: जनसंहार. Example: The international court prosecuted several leaders for genocide. Other options: Uxoricide = the killing of one's wife; Sororicide = the killing of one's sister; Regicide = the killing of a king.
Particular types or categories of literature or art

Genre = Particular types or categories of literature or art. Hindi: शैली. Example: Crime fiction is the genre she finds most gripping to read. Gentry = People of high social status. Hindi: कुलीन वर्ग. Example: The local gentry attended the annual charity ball in considerable number. Other options: Laudable = worthy of high praise; Genesis = beginning or origin of something; Usurer = one who lends money at high interest rates.
The study of the earth's physical features, climate and population

Geography = The study of the earth's physical features, climate and population. Hindi: भूगोल. Example: Geography classes helped students understand the physical features of the earth. Other options: Topography = features (such as mountains and rivers) in an area of land; Geologist = A person who studies the structure of the earth; Cosmography = science of the constitution of the whole universe.

Geologist = A person who studies the structure of the earth. Hindi: भूविज्ञानी. Example: The geologist examined the rock strata to determine the age of the formation. The study of rocks and soil

Geology = The study of rocks and soil. Hindi: भूविज्ञान. Example: His study of geology revealed layers of rock deposited over millions of years. Other options: Archaeology = the study of the ancient and recent human past through material remains; Cytology = the study of cells; Neurology = the study of nerves.
A state, society, or group governed by old people

Gerontocracy = A state, society, or group governed by old people. Hindi: वृद्धतंत्र. Example: Critics described the ruling council as a gerontocracy, with no leader under seventy. Study of various aspects of ageing

Gerontology = Study of various aspects of ageing. Hindi: वृद्धावस्था विज्ञान. Example: Gerontology has become increasingly important as global populations age. A movement of part of the body to express an idea or feeling

Gesture = A movement of part of the body to express an idea or feeling. Hindi: इशारा. Example: She made a gesture of goodwill by returning the lost wallet without expecting a reward. Parts of cities in which members of a particular group or race live usually in poor conditions

Vernacular = Language of ordinary speech rather than formal writing. Hindi: स्थानीय भाषा. Example: The poem was written in the local vernacular, using dialect words that standard dictionaries do not record. Other options: Parlance = language used by a particular group of people; Articulation = formations of clear and distinct sounds in speech; Biography = writing of one's life story.
Able to do many different things

Versatile = Able to do many different things. Hindi: बहुमुखी. Example: The versatile actor performed equally well in comedy and tragedy. Other options: Motley = made up of many different people or things; Collage = collection of things, which may be similar or different; Potpourri = collection of different things.

Vespers = Evening prayer in church. Hindi: गिरजा में सायंकालीन उपासना. Example: The monks gathered for vespers as the sun went down behind the hills. Other options: Aspersion = an attack on the reputation and integrity of someone or something; Spokesperson = one who speaks on behalf of others; Whisper = speak in a very low tone.

Viable = That will be successful. Hindi: व्यवहार्य. Example: Several viable alternatives to the proposed route were put forward for consideration. Other options: Insatiable = that which can not be satisfied; Fable = A short story with a moral lesson; Potable = safe to drink.
Feelings that someone or something gives you

Vibe = Feelings that someone or something gives you. Hindi: अनुभूति. Example: The restaurant had a relaxed, friendly vibe that made everyone feel welcome. Other options: Sensitive = aware of and able to understand other people and their feelings; Euphoria = feelings of great happiness and excitement; Acrimonious = full of anger, arguments and bad feelings.
An area around or near a particular place

Vicinity = An area around or near a particular place. Hindi: आस-पास. Example: Police searched the entire vicinity of the explosion for clues. Other options: Meadow = an area of grassland where animals graze; Quagmire = an area of soft, wet ground; situation that is hard to deal with or…; Purview = an area within which someone or something has authority, influence, or knowledge.
Saying or writing very harsh and critical things about (someone or something)

Vilify = Saying or writing very harsh and critical things about (someone or something). Hindi: बदनाम करना. Example: Newspapers continued to vilify the accused even before the trial had begun. Other options: Obloquy = harsh or critical statements about someone; Exegesis = critical explanation or interpretation of a scripture; Vitriolic = full of bitter, harsh and angry criticism.
Person who portrays bad character roles in cinema

Villain = Person who portrays bad character roles in cinema. Hindi: खलनायक. Example: The villain of the piece turned out to be the character everyone had trusted most. Other options: Plaintiff = person who files a suit; Matinee = A cinema show held in the afternoon; Profile = general view of a person's character.
To show or state that someone or something is not guilty of something

Vindicate = To show or state that someone or something is not guilty of something. Hindi: निर्दोष सिद्ध करना. Example: The evidence finally served to vindicate the accused, clearing his name completely. Other options: Relocate = moving to a new place; Exonerate = declare someone not guilty or free from blame; Syndicate = groups of people or businesses that work together.
Having or showing a desire to hurt someone who has hurt or caused problems for you

Vindictive = Having or showing a desire to hurt someone who has hurt or caused problems for you. Hindi: प्रतिशोधी. Example: Her vindictive campaign against her former colleague damaged both of their reputations. Other options: Erudite = having or showing knowledge that is learned by studying; Plucky = having or showing a lot of courage or determination; Gory = having or showing a lot of violence and blood.
Very close to being something without actually being it

Virtual = Very close to being something without actually being it. Hindi: आभासी. Example: Remote working has created a virtual office environment for many employees. Other options: Hypocrisy = behaviour in which somebody pretends to have moral standards or opinions that they do…; Replica = exact or very close copy of something; Transonic = relating to speeds close to that of sound.
One who possesses outstanding technical ability in a particular art or field

Virtuoso = One who possesses outstanding technical ability in a particular art or field. Hindi: कलाप्रवीण व्यक्ति. Example: The young violinist was already regarded as a virtuoso at the age of sixteen. Other options: Cynosure = one who is a centre of attraction; Visionary = one who can think about the future with imagination and wisdom; Insolvent = one who is unable to pay his debts.
Full of hate or anger, extremely or excessively harsh or strong

Virulent = Full of hate or anger, extremely or excessively harsh or strong. Hindi: विषैला. Example: A virulent strain of the virus spread rapidly through the school. Other options: Indolent = not liking to work or be active; Truculent = easily annoyed or angered and likely to argue; Outcry = expressions of strong anger or disapproval by many people.

Viticulture = The cultivation of grapes. Hindi: अंगूर की खेती. Example: The region's long tradition of viticulture produced some of the finest wines in Europe. Other options: Caricature = A picture of a person or thing drawn in an exaggerated manner to cause…; Conjecture = an opinion or conclusion formed on the basis of incomplete information; Venture = new activities, projects, business, etc., that typically involve risk.
Full of bitter, harsh and angry criticism

Vitriolic = Full of bitter, harsh and angry criticism. Hindi: कटु. Example: His vitriolic review destroyed the restaurant's reputation overnight. Other options: Obloquy = harsh or critical statements about someone; Melancholic = feeling or expressing pensive sadness; Diatribe = bitter and violent attack in words.
Blaming or insulting (someone) in strong or violent language

Vituperate = Blaming or insulting (someone) in strong or violent language. Hindi: निंदा करना. Example: She would vituperate anyone who questioned her methods. Other options: Fixation = A strong interest in something or someone; Conglomerate = large business that is made of different kinds of companies; Adulterate = make impure by adding inferior substances.
Expressing feelings or opinions in a very loud or forceful way

Vociferous = Expressing feelings or opinions in a very loud or forceful way. Hindi: मुखर. Example: The vociferous crowd made it almost impossible to hear the referee's decisions. Other options: Pestiferous = that which is morally dangerous; Herbivorous = an animal that feeds on plants; Onerous = difficult and unpleasant to do or deal with.

Void = Having no legal power. Hindi: अमान्य. Example: The judge declared the contract void, as it lacked the necessary legal authority. Other options: Judiciary = the part of a country's government responsible for its legal system; Nondescript = having no distinctive or interesting features; Bona Fide = genuine, real or legal; not false.
Likely to change in a very sudden or extreme way; likely to become dangerous or out of control

Volatile = Likely to change in a very sudden or extreme way; likely to become dangerous or out of control. Hindi: परिवर्तनशील. Example: The volatile political situation made investment in the region extremely risky. Other options: Volte Face = complete change of attitude or opinion; Menace = A person or thing that is likely to cause harm; Tactile = of or concerned with sense of touch.
The faculty or power of using one's will

Volition = The faculty or power of using one's will. Hindi: इच्छाशक्ति. Example: He left the position entirely of his own volition, with no pressure from above. Other options: Abduction = forcing someone to go somewhere with you, often using threats or violence; Transition = changing from one state or condition to another; Dereliction = an act of no longer caring for, using, or doing something, failure to do….
Complete change of attitude or opinion

Volte Face = Complete change of attitude or opinion. Hindi: पूरी तरह पलट जाना. Example: His volte face on the issue surprised even his closest allies. Other options: Omnipotent = having complete or unlimited power; Volatile = likely to change in a very sudden or extreme way; likely to become dangerous…; Preface = introduction to a book or speech.
Done or given because one wants to and not because one is forced to

Voluntary = Done or given because one wants to and not because one is forced to. Hindi: स्वैच्छिक. Example: Attendance at the extra sessions was entirely voluntary. Other options: Rudimentary = not very developed or advanced; Refugee = A person who has been forced to leave his country because there is a…; Tributary = stream flowing into another big river.
Attractive in a sensual way; having a full, curvy figure (of a woman)

Voluptuous = Attractive in a sensual way; having a full, curvy figure (of a woman). Hindi: कामुक. Example: The still life painting featured voluptuous fruit arranged in a stone bowl. Other options: Sumptuous = splendid and expensive-looking; Voluntary = done or given because one wants to and not because one is forced to; Tumultuous = involving a lot of violence, confusion, or disorder.
Having a very eager appetite; greedy

Voracious = Having a very eager appetite; greedy. Hindi: पेटू. Example: He was a voracious reader, consuming three or four books each week. Other options: Rapacious = greedy for money; Vivacious = happy and lively in a way that is attractive; Sagacious = having or showing an ability to understand difficult ideas and situations and to make….
Long journeys to a distant or unknown place especially over water or through outer space

Voyage = Long journeys to a distant or unknown place especially over water or through outer space. Hindi: जलयात्रा. Example: The voyage across the Pacific took forty-seven days in the small yacht. Other options: Tirade = long and angry speech; Bon Voyage = said to somebody who is leaving on a journey, to wish them a good…; Foundling = an abandoned child of unknown parents found by others.
Not having or showing good manners, good taste, or politeness

Vulgar = Not having or showing good manners, good taste, or politeness. Hindi: अशिष्ट. Example: His vulgar remarks at the formal dinner shocked the other guests. Other options: Virtue = ethically good behaviour one has; Ambiguous = not having one obvious meaning; Indiscreet = not having or showing good judgment.
Open to attack, harm, or damage

Vulnerable = Open to attack, harm, or damage. Hindi: असुरक्षित. Example: The elderly are particularly vulnerable during periods of extreme heat. Other options: Eradicable = which can be rooted out; Parable = story told to illustrate a moral or spiritual truth; Innocuous = causing no harm.
A long, thin stick used by a magician or in magic tricks

Wand = A long, thin stick used by a magician or in magic tricks. Hindi: छड़ी. Example: The magician waved his wand and the rabbit disappeared from the hat. Other options: Wily = full of clever tricks; Pestle = stick with a thick end used in a mortar for pounding; Thrash = hitting (someone or something) very hard with a stick, whip, etc.
A large, tall cupboard in which clothes may be hung or stored

Wardrobe = A large, tall cupboard in which clothes may be hung or stored. Hindi: कपड़े की अलमारी. Example: She opened the wardrobe and selected a suit for the morning meeting. Other options: Horde = A large group of people; Aviary = A large cage, building, or enclosure to keep birds; Dormitory = A large bedroom for a number of people in a school or institution.
A list of passengers and luggage

Waybill = A list of passengers and luggage. Hindi: यात्री की सूची. Example: The driver checked the waybill to confirm all items were accounted for before leaving the depot. Other options: Walkway = A raised passageway in a building; Inventory = A detailed list of things in a place; Waterfall = A steep descent of water from a stream or river.
Speak in a very low tone

Whisper = Speak in a very low tone. Hindi: फुसफुसाना. Example: She leaned over to whisper the answer to her classmate during the test. Other options: Delirium = mental states in which one is confused and not able to think or speak…; Decadence = behaviour that shows low morals and a great love of pleasure, money, fame, etc; Whine = the sound of mosquitoes.
Reduce something in size by gradual series of steps

Whittle = Reduce something in size by gradual series of steps. Hindi: छाँटना. Example: The campaign manager worked to whittle the shortlist down from twenty to five candidates. Other options: Slacken = reduce or decrease in speed or intensity; Whisk = to take someone somewhere suddenly and quickly; Whisper = speak in a very low tone.
A man whose wife is dead

Widower = A man whose wife is dead. Hindi: विदुर. Example: The widower found it difficult to adapt to living alone after forty years of marriage. Other options: Henpeck = A man who is controlled by his wife; Polygamist = A person having more than one wife at the same time; Effeminate = A man who is womanish in his habits.

Wily = Full of clever tricks. Hindi: चतुर. Example: The wily negotiator always had a fallback position concealed until the last moment. Other options: Wand = A long, thin stick used by a magician or in magic tricks; Wry = humorous in a clever and often ironic way; Repartee = conversations in which clever statements and replies are made quickly.
To separate husk from the grain

Winnow = To separate husk from the grain. Hindi: फटकना. Example: The farmer used a fan to winnow the wheat from the chaff. Other options: Windfall = an unexpected piece of good fortune; Widower = A man whose wife is dead; Scatter = cause (things or people) to separate and go in different directions.

Witchery = The practice of magic. Hindi: जादू-टोना. Example: The stage magician's act was full of apparent witchery that baffled even sceptical audience members. Other options: Bigamy = the practice of having two spouses at the same time; Lexicography = the practice of writing dictionaries; Debauchery = bad or immoral behaviour that involves sex, drugs, alcohol, etc.

Witty = Funny and clever. Hindi: विनोदपूर्ण. Example: Her witty observations about office life made the book an immediate bestseller. Other options: Outsmart = defeating or tricking (someone) by being more intelligent or clever; Witch = A woman who is thought to have magic powers; Nitty Gritty = most important and basic facts or details about something.
An argument that is complicated and continues over a long period of time

Wrangle = An argument that is complicated and continues over a long period of time. Hindi: झगड़ा. Example: The inheritance wrangle dragged on through the courts for over a decade. Other options: Saga = long and complicated series of events; Bungle = carry out a task clumsily or incompetently; Quadrangle = A court or open space usually rectangular and enclosed by a building.
An arrangement of leaves, flowers, fruits, etc., in the shape of a circle that is used for decoration

Wreath = An arrangement of leaves, flowers, fruits, etc., in the shape of a circle that is used for decoration. Hindi: पुष्पचक्र. Example: A wreath of poppies was placed at the base of the war memorial. Other options: Bequeath = leaving (property) to a person or other beneficiary by a will; Ornate = covered with decoration; Chronology = an arrangement of events or dates in the order of their occurrence.
The remains of something that has been badly damaged

Wreckage = The remains of something that has been badly damaged. Hindi: मलबा. Example: The rescue team searched through the wreckage after the plane crash. Other options: Fossil = the hard remains of a prehistoric animal or plant found inside rock; Archaeology = the study of the ancient and recent human past through material remains; Outlaw = A person who has broken the law, especially one who remains at large or….
To move along with quick, short twisting movements

Wriggle = To move along with quick, short twisting movements. Hindi: छटपटाना. Example: The suspect tried to wriggle out of his responsibilities by blaming his subordinates. Other options: Temporary = lasting only for a very short while; Symphony = A long musical composition for a full orchestra, usually in several movements; Ephemeral = lasting for a very short time.

Xenophobia = Fear or dislike of foreigners. Hindi: विदेशियों से घृणा. Example: Rising xenophobia led to discrimination against immigrants. Other options: Algophobia = fear of pain; Aerophobia = fear of flying; Ophiophobia = fear of snakes.
Used to express excitement or joy

Yahoo = Used to express excitement or joy. Hindi: याहू. Example: He let out a loud yahoo when told he had passed the examination. Other options: Aflutter = in a state of tremulous excitement; Casting Couch = used to refer to a process in which actors are chosen for a film…; Eureka = used to express excitement when a discovery has been made.
A feeling of intense longing for something

Yearning = A feeling of intense longing for something. Hindi: तड़प. Example: There was a deep yearning in his voice as he spoke about the country he had left behind. Other options: Nostalgia = A sentimental longing or wistful affection for a period in the past; Abate = become less intense or widespread; Blitzkrieg = intense military campaign intended to bring about a swift victory.
Farmers in the past who owned a small amount of land

Yeoman = Farmers in the past who owned a small amount of land. Hindi: छोटा किसान. Example: The old yeoman family had farmed the same land for five generations. Other options: Flagship = best or most important thing owned or produced by a particular organisation; Theomania = religious madness; Horizon = the line where sky and land meet.

Zenith = The highest point. Hindi: शीर्षबिंदु. Example: The empire was at the zenith of its power during the reign of its third ruler. Other options: Zealot = A person who is fanatical and uncompromising in pursuit of religious or political ideals; Crescendo = the loudest point of a period of continuous noise; Zest = feelings of enjoyment and enthusiasm.

Zoophobia = Fear of animals. Hindi: पशुभीति. Example: Her zoophobia made it impossible for her to visit the zoo with her children. Other options: Microphobia = fear of small things; Algophobia = fear of pain; Bibliophobia = fear of books.
